events.title: The death of St. Birinus, apostle of Wessex
events.shortBlurb: Sent by Pope Honorius to the heathen West Saxons, the first bishop of Dorchester died about the middle of the seventh century and was buried in his own cathedral city…
body: Birinus, a priest of Rome, asked of Pope Honorius I leave to preach the gospel to the idolaters of Britain; the pope commended his zeal and caused him to be ordained bishop. Landing in the kingdom of the West Saxons about 634, he found the people still pagan and stayed.

He baptized King Cynegils, the sixth in descent from Cerdic, who had founded the kingdom in 519, and with him many of his people; the king gave him for his see the Roman town of Dorcis, now Dorchester on the Thames. There he built and consecrated many churches and gained many souls to God.

He died on 3 December, in a year variously reckoned as 649 or 650, and was buried in the same city; Bishop Hedda afterward translated his remains to Winchester. The sees of Salisbury, Exeter, Wells, Worcester, Lichfield, and Hereford were afterward formed out of his single bishopric of Dorchester, itself soon transferred to Winchester, so that he is rightly named the apostle of Wessex.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 3 December
